name: Religious Orders
summary: The clergy of the Chorus and the minor deities. Each order serves its god's aspects; none commands universal worship since the Sundering. Orders are listed with their deity, temperament, and current concerns in year 812 AA.

orders.name: The Halo Priesthood
orders.summary: Judges, oath-keepers, and temple-wardens of the ringed sun. They swear magistrates into office and witness coronations.
orders.current_concern: The Year of Ashfall has filled the Halos with refugees praying for justice; the priesthood quietly debates whether Solvane's silence is judgment or absence.

orders.name: The Moonwardens
orders.summary: Keepers of calendars, debts, and birthings. Every town's ledger dates from its Moonwarden's arrival.
orders.current_concern: Birth-records are the Censer's chief hunting tool — and the Moonwardens keep them. Some wardens have begun to falsify entries; others report them.

orders.name: The Deep-Shapers
orders.summary: Orbren's priests: artisans, miners, masons. The only order whose deity every species names the same.
orders.current_concern: The deep-folk holds report the Stone Crown 'ringing' — the same note the Storm-Bound hear at sea. The Shapers have sealed three shafts and said nothing.

orders.name: The Verdant Kin
orders.summary: Druids of the old greenwood and field-priests of the harvest. Human kin serve farmland; greenfolk kin serve the Greenwood proper.
orders.current_concern: Glimmer-sickness appears in crops near the Quiet's edge. The Kin purge what they can and beg the Root-Wardens for guidance that does not come.

orders.name: The Veil-Keepers
orders.summary: Funeral rites and last vows. The Stilleven vigil is theirs; so is the duty of naming the dead when no one else will.
orders.current_concern: More bodies than names since Ashfall. And one grave in the Crownlands that will not stay filled.

orders.name: The Road-Singers
orders.summary: Jesters, gamblers, guides, and the unofficial postal service of Aurelith. Welcome everywhere, trusted nowhere.
orders.current_concern: A Road-Singer ballad about the Year of Ashfall is spreading faster than any song should — it contains details no singer could know.

orders.name: The Glass-Keepers
orders.summary: Tenders of the buried Concord cities' mouths in the Ashlands and the desert glass. Small, grim, and unwelcome everywhere official.
orders.current_concern: The glass is ringing too. The Keepers have begun marking new cracks on maps already dense with them.

orders.name: The Deep-Wardens
orders.summary: Guardians of the innermost groves where the old song sleeps. Greenfolk-only; strangers who enter do not return changed so much as returned.
orders.current_concern: Something is waking in the deepest grove. The Wardens have not told the Root-Wardens — or anyone.

orders.name: The Oath-Sept
orders.summary: Minor clerks of lawful succession, betrothal, and land disputes in the Crownlands. Tolerated by the court, ignored by the Halos.
orders.current_concern: Three council seats fall due next election. The Sept's ledgers show two candidates' lineages contain convenient impossibilities.

orders.name: The Veil-Wardens
orders.summary: Scholars who map the Quiet's advance for the Reeve's court. The Censer denies their existence; the court funds them anyway.
orders.current_concern: Their newest map shows the Quiet advancing toward Velkash's aquifer. The court has sat on the report for a month.

orders.name: The First-Heard Sect
orders.summary: A heresy within the Censer itself: incense-bearers who believe the returning Glimmer is a second chance. Young, growing, and watched.
orders.current_concern: The Nine Ashes vote on the sect's purge within the season. Someone inside the sect has begun leaking archive locations to the Rememberers.

orders.name: The Well-Sisters
orders.summary: Keepers of the deep wells and spring-oases of the Burning Sands. The desert's quiet arbiters; poisoning a well is the one crime they punish themselves.
orders.current_concern: A well turned to salt last month — the first in living memory. The Sisters do not believe Akhmat did it.
